items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Business logic uses cryptic short names throughout swscale_process: s0, ss0, d0, ds0, sw, sh, dw, dh, sfmt, dfmt. Some comments map branches to workloads ("YUV -> RGB with scaling (b005/s004...)"), but most of the file has little documentation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One main.zig of about 130KB holds everything. swscale_process is far over 100 lines and repeats the NV12/NV21 deinterleave and scratch-offset blocks in several branches. The diff also commits .zig-cache/ and zig-out/libswscale_candidate.so.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Scratch is carved with manual offsets (ctx.scratch[scratch_offset .. +plane_sz]) and checked only at build time; ReleaseFast removes the runtime bounds checks. It uses the magic alignment (x+15)&~15 and returns -1 at the end of swscale_process with no error detail.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: The hidden correctness test failed ("output does not meet the accuracy bars") even though the agent saw 58/58 locally. That points to geometry/format cases beyond the contract sizes. Intermediates are packed into scratch at width-sized stride, and the 422/444 path is chosen by comparing dst_cw == dw.
